result:
The overnight job now fingerprints saved metrics the same way the readers do, so results for metrics with per-experiment breakdowns are stored under the key the readers look up. I didn't run tests or add one, as instructed.

**Cause:** `_get_experiment_saved_metrics_for_hour_sync` in `posthog/temporal/experiments/activities.py` fingerprinted the raw `saved_metric.query`. Breakdowns live on the experiment's link to the metric (`ExperimentToSavedMetric.metadata`), and the batch calculation applies them when it runs the query. So results were computed with the breakdowns but stored under a fingerprint that left them out. The timeseries sync, the cold-start fallback and the results chart all fingerprint the query merged with its breakdowns, so they never found those rows.

**Fix:** the discovery step now fingerprints `merge_saved_metric_breakdowns(saved_metric.query, exp_to_saved_metric.metadata)`. That is the same merge `iter_metric_dicts` uses on the read side. Metrics without breakdowns hash as before, because `compute_metric_fingerprint` already treats an empty breakdown filter the same as none.

To let the activity import the helper, I renamed `_merge_saved_metric_breakdowns` to `merge_saved_metric_breakdowns` in `temporal/metric_resolution.py` and re-exported it from `facade/timeseries.py`. I also updated the docstring reference in `experiment_metric_fingerprint.py`.

Saved metrics with breakdowns will get new fingerprints from this change, so any rows the old fingerprint left behind are orphaned. Those results were never being read anyway.
